battery.NB-1.1: the population's inscriptions in the layer's own numbering and segmentation; sequences are the rows' sign sequences from the pinned layer; no re-segmentation, renumbering, or crosswalk is applied to any sign at any point
battery.NB-1.2: position classes initial (first sign), terminal (last sign), medial (every other occurrence), for sequences of length >= 2; sequences of length 1 are counted and reported separately and enter no count; every counted occurrence falls in exactly one class (partition property: initial + terminal + medial counts sum to the sequence-length total over sequences of length >= 2)
battery.NB-1.3: per sign s and class c: count n_c(s) and total N(s) over sequences of length >= 2; rate r_c(s) = n_c(s) / N(s); counts and rates both reported
battery.NB-1.4: a sign is classifiable iff N(s) >= 20 (basis: the smallest total among the ten exhibited Phase-43 TERMINAL_STRONG signs is 22; the floor admits signs of that order at rate resolution 1/20 = 0.05; explicitly not a recovered Phase-43 value)
battery.NB-1.5: for classifiable signs: TERMINAL_STRONG iff r_terminal >= 2/3; TERMINAL_MODERATE iff 1/2 <= r_terminal < 2/3; INITIAL_ and MEDIAL_ by the same bands on their rates (basis: 2/3 sits just below the lowest exhibited Phase-43 TERMINAL_STRONG rate, 0.683, exhibited range 0.683-0.892, so the frozen Phase-43 strong set passes the consistency check against this band; the initial/medial bands are the same numbers by symmetry, a labelled design choice)
battery.NB-1.6: opening bigrams: the first two signs of each sequence of length >= 2; dominance of a pair = its count / B, where B = the number of sequences of length >= 2 (this repairs the Phase-43 record's denominator-less 0.74 and its self-contradiction on the (267, 99) count)
battery.NB-1.7: chance baseline: a within-sequence permutation null (each sequence's length and sign multiset fixed, order uniformly permuted), 999 permutations, seed 43052, over the primary population; the chance level of a statistic is its nearest-rank 95th percentile across the 999 values (the 950th smallest); statistics: the TERMINAL_STRONG count and the maximum opening-bigram dominance
battery.NB-1.8: condition F: at least one TERMINAL_STRONG sign exists AND the observed TERMINAL_STRONG count exceeds its NB-1.7 chance level. Condition O: the top opening bigram's count is at least 10 AND its dominance exceeds its NB-1.7 chance level (the count floor of 10 is a stated design choice of this amendment)
battery.NB-1.9: TOO THIN gate: fewer than 30 sequences of length >= 3 in the primary population, or fewer than 10 classifiable signs, closes the run TOO THIN before conditions F and O are evaluated

design.outcome_semantics: amendment.md sec.6, claim F052-C19: CONSISTENT iff neither condition F nor condition O holds on the primary population (the Farmer pattern present in the CISI-lineage corpus too; the recorded caveat narrows); INCONSISTENT iff both hold (the caveat widens); PARTIAL (DD-052-3, retained) iff exactly one holds, the outcome naming which; TOO THIN is gate D's closure.
